Children, young people and adults living within the Tees Valley Area and wider North East region through sporting and positive health activities. The Tees Valley area is made up of Local Authority locations-Stockton-on-Tees, Middlesbrough, Hartlepool & Redcar & Cleveland. Each of these LAO's has a high concentration of communities that experience health & socio-economic inequalities. Stockton-on-Tees has one of the largest national health inequality gaps in the UK-reflecting great internal disparities - the gap in life expectancy between 2 neighbouring postcodes in Stockton within 1 mile of each other the gap was 15.2 years less in the more deprived area. Middlesbrough has the highest rates of rising child poverty of any town in the UK and the poorest health outcomes for lung related health nationally. Children in deprived areas are 15% more likely to experience childhood obesity & related health issues, in comparison to those in more affluent areas. Some of the Wards in the Tees Valley are the most deprived wards in the country so the need for assets to tackle this statistic is significant. Hartlepool & Redcar & Cleveland are also 2 of the most deprived local authorities nationally-both featuring in the top 10 most deprived LAO's in England (along with Middlesbrough) in the 2019 'Indices of Deprivation' report. These 4 LAO's -with significant levels of health deprivation, socio economic deprivation and child poverty- which make up the 'Tees Valley' area-are the geographical area & communities that 'On your turf sports' would seek to serve. With the main purpose of business being to support individuals, groups and organisations to achieve access to sports in 'their space'. There are many existing spaces & resources available in these areas that encourage health & fitness. However, we are conscious that they are not being accessed by those who need them the most and therefore the current trend for increasing inequality & deprivation is unlikely to shift-unless a new approach is adopted. We recognize that the multiple barriers to accessing a healthy lifestyle and fitness do not just relate to the existence of provision/venue or service. Instead they relate to 'accessibility and engagement'. These 2 key components are what 'On Your Turf sports' will seek to address and support. This will be done through the use of multiple, combined decades of experience & knowledge between our team-in relation to engaging with disadvantaged communities, supporting physical & mental health & wellbeing, tackling social issues and improving social mobility. We forsee that 'On Your Turf Sports' will support multiple local & national agendas-including:  Tackling Diabetes (greatest strain on NHS aside from coronary related health)  Tackling respiratory health (our region is one of worst affected areas in UK)  Tackling social isolation Youth loneliness is a huge issue-particularly amongst children and  Pro actively engaging young people with SEND & BEMH related issues.  Promoting positive mental health through physical activity-'On Your Turf' & 'On Your terms' (meaning-in the service is brought to the person & is bespoke to their needs)  Tackling increasing Suicide rates-Teesside has one of the highest suicide rates in the UK and Stockton-on-Tees has a high rate of teenage suicide and reported poor mental health amongst it's younger population. 'On Your Turf Sports' will seek to do this via the provision of free sports access to those who need it the most-through the means of providing mobile sporting equipment/facilities in local neighbourhoods & communities-that we already know and connect with. This service will meet unmet needs that we have identified, observed & experienced in our existing roles as community & youth workers. Needs that are reflected in the data sets referenced above.

Further community sporting/health activities for our beneficiaries Supporting the agendas of other local & national providers-other local charities, schools, NHS services.

The Croft @ Crook CIC will embark on a three-phase development plan that encompasses the acquisition and renovation of the building, the facilitation of its management and profitable operation, and the reinvestment of revenue from all activities into a diverse array of arts and culture programs, digital skills and employability training, as well as health and well-being workshops delivered by local providers in an accessible facility at significantly subsidized costs.

name: PENSART CIC
description:
The company will have 2 functions:  1. The development and maintenance of an online arts platform for visual art, spoken word pieces and social commentary works. The platform will also develop audiovisual content and provide social engagement through gastronomy and other cultural activities. This platform is designed for people in the UK and abroad who look to improve their wellbeing through an engagement with culture. Specific audiences within this broad description include retired people and foreigners who have settled in the UK.  2. The provision of bespoke English language learning opportunities. The company will also provide educational support services. The main audience for these services are non English speakers in the UK and abroad. The main focus is asylum seekers, refugees and people with settled status who need a better level of English to integrate and get jobs.

Any surplus will be used to provide extra English language lessons, build the arts space online and reach out to more artists, writers and broadcasters.

name: WE DO UNFILTERED LIVES CIC
description:
The company will operate for the benefit of individuals affected by addiction, trauma, and mental health challenges, including those in active recovery, their families, and the wider community. This includes people with lived experience of substance misuse, social isolation, or emotional distress who are seeking holistic and person-centred support. The company will also support families and caregivers affected by addiction, and contribute to building stronger, healthier, and more connected communities in Hartlepool and the wider Tees Valley region.

Any surplus generated by the company will be reinvested back into the organisation to support and benefit the community.

name: GENEVA FOUNDATION CIC
description:
Individuals and communities across the UK with an interest in brass band music, particularly: - Young people, including those from disadvantaged backgrounds, who will benefit from access to musical education, mentorship, and opportunities to develop self-discipline, confidence, and teamwork through collective music-making. - Ex-military service personnel, particularly former military bandsmen, by offering them meaningful pathways to reintegrate into civilian life through roles in education, performance, and community outreach within the brass band world. - The wider public, especially in regions with historic links to brass bands (e.g. former mining and industrial communities), through increased access to performances, workshops, and educational events that celebrate and preserve the UK’s rich brass band heritage.  The Geneva Foundation CIC is committed to reducing and/or removing socio economic barriers to participation in the brass band tradition — whether financial, geographic, or social — ensuring that this unique musical culture remains vibrant, relevant, and accessible to all. In doing so, it fosters social inclusion, lifelong learning, and cultural pride, while creating new community networks rooted in shared musical experience.

Any surplus income will go into supporting initiatives supporting the sustainability of the rich heritage of Brass Banding in the UK

name: NEWTOWN ROOTS CIC
description:
The company is established to benefit people experiencing homelessness in and around the Stockton area, in particular those who are rough sleeping, sofa surfing, or facing imminent eviction.  Our core activities will include providing emergency accommodation, access to basic hygiene facilities and connecting individuals with health and social care services.  We will also offer advocacy, job training, and support in securing permanent housing.  Through these activities, our aim is to improve safety, wellbeing and prospects for homeless individuals, reducing the risks associated with rough sleeping and social exclusion.

Any surplus generated will be reinvested to expand our services and reach more people in need.

name: REBIRTH INITIATIVE CIC
description:
Individuals across the Tees Valley who face barriers to employment and social inclusion, particularly those connected to local churches and community groups.  Rebirth Initiative CIC will deliver tailored employability support including skills workshops, CV writing clinics, interview preparation, and confidence-building sessions. These activities will be grounded in Christian values of dignity, purpose, and compassion, helping participants to rebuild their lives, find meaningful work, and reintegrate into society

Any surplus made by the company will be reinvested into the development and delivery of employability programmes, training sessions, and community outreach activities across Teesside. Surplus may also be donated to other organisations that support similar community benefit objectives, with the consent of the CIC Regulator if such organisations are not nominated Asset Locked Bodies.

name: MEADOWCROFT SUPPORTED HOUSING CIC
description:
The Company’s activities will provide benefit to vulnerable adults within the community by providing them supported accommodation and tenancy care, support and supervision.

If any surplus is generated this will be used to provide extra services to tenants such as training and workshops to equip them with life skills that will help them start to build confidence in sustaining an independent tenancy - e.g. cooking courses, maintenance and handyman courses etc.  Also it is our intention that we then start to use any further surplus to provide our own supported accommodation properties for such tenants.
